instruction: Use Abaqus through the graphical user interface to perform a tensile analysis of a thin rectangular shell plate with a central circular hole. Use the N-mm-MPa unit system. Model Definition: Build a 3D Deformable Shell part consisting of a 120 mm by 240 mm rectangular plate on the XY plane with a central 12 mm diameter circular hole centered at (60, 120) mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Steel with Young's modulus E = 210000 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.3. Create a Homogeneous Shell Section with a thickness of 1 mm and 5 through-thickness integration points, and assign it to the entire plate. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the shell plate. Analysis Step: Define a Static, General step named Step-HoleTension with the Initial step as its predecessor. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply opposing tensile shell edge loads of 8 N/mm to the vertical edges: on the left edge at X = 0 in the negative X direction, and on the right edge at X = 120 in the positive X direction. Constrain the plate to prevent rigid-body motion without over-constraining the tensile deformation: - Fix U1 = U2 = U3 = 0 at the bottom-left corner (0, 0). - Fix U2 = U3 = 0 at the bottom-right corner (120, 0). - Fix U3 = 0 at the top-left corner (0, 240). Discretization: Mesh the plate using S4R shell elements. Apply a local seed size of approximately 2.4 mm to the hole edge and a global seed size of 10 mm to the remainder of the plate. Job Execution: Create and submit a job named Job-FlangeHole. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.cae and ensure the output database is written to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-FlangeHole.odb. Run the solver to completion and ensure a result file is generated. You must complete all operations interactively through the abaqus graphical user interface (GUI) step by step. The use of external script files is strictly prohibited.
